note: Reuses the exact real hardware boundary established in Phase 12B (results/phase12/kv-device-override/pressure_test.json): SmolLM2-360M, ctx=200000, GTX 1650. At this context, full-GPU KV allocation genuinely FAILS (real, hard allocation error) while a 16/16 CPU/GPU KV split SUCCEEDS, with weights unchanged (mp.n_gpu_layers=-1, all 32 weight layers Vulkan1-resident in both cases). Phase 12C adds: does a manual promotion of a CPU-KV group work in this exact constrained regime, without destabilizing the host?
answer: Yes: a manual promotion of a CPU-KV group can be temporarily executed in this exact constrained regime (ctx=200000, where full-GPU KV hard-fails) without destabilizing the host -- byte-correct, weights remained GPU-resident throughout, and process/host were stable. This is the SAME classification-B copy-only mechanism as everywhere else in this phase, now confirmed to also work at the real memory-pressure boundary, not just at comfortable low-ctx configs.
